answer: A proof produced for one use is bound to that use by a challenge the prover could not have anticipated when it was created, so the work cannot be computed once and replayed across a fleet, and every use demands a fresh unpredictable input. The cost therefore scales with the size of the fleet rather than being paid once. Every use pulls an echo, signs an onyx against it, and the umber guarantees the onyx was not ready in advance: the fleet can copy keys but never an echo it did not receive in the moment. Recording and replaying is exactly what the challenge defeats.
